reason: The text says which node writes which existing escalation reason, and the tests check exactly that.
The task describes the closed panel staying mounted with the hidden attribute and the queryAllByRole change, which is what the tests check.
Swapping the header email link for a GitHub link uses the existing GitHub handle and href from portfolioData, and target/rel follow the repo's external-link convention.
The task names line 7 as no AI attribution, and the tests check natural cases (co-author and session trailers, generated-by footers) through the existing check()/readFile interface.
The tests check the described behaviour: scroll to (0,0) on a new-page link, but not on first render, hash links or going back.
The task quotes the fictional-data label and describes clearing the timers; the new render tests read existing data.
Ending a torn last line before appending is described clearly, and the tests check that behaviour, not names or strings.
LF-only appends and skipping blank ledger lines are stated directly, and the tests check that behaviour.
The tests check the described behaviour: focus moves to the first phase tab after Back to the start, and the autoplay block is unchanged.
The text names answers_by_prompt_marker, the line-start marker rule, the 'Actions already applied:' marker and the postmortem queue, which is what the tests check.
Matching keywords at the start of a name word is exactly what the tests check (prefix of a `_`-separated token).
Tests check 403 for cross-origin POSTs, 400 for a malformed session id, and that bad JSON lines and one failing transcript reader do not stop the watcher, all described in the task.
The text gives the torn_ledger_lines name, the last-line-only rule, the error for earlier lines and the lenient decoding, which match what the tests check.
The task names the request field timeouts and the metric lodestar_model_timeouts_total, and the agent label follows the existing metric pattern.
Cutting the verdict section makes the next section 'trust' the replay's skip target, and both ids already exist in the data.
Reading the approved plan from the main checkout when inside a stale worktree is stated clearly and is what the test checks.
Removing .pdf from BINARY_EXTENSIONS, as the task says, leaves the list the test expects.
The task gives the {"error": ...} shape for the cap and database figures, the 200 body and the /metrics behaviour that the test checks.

The title-only task says what to do (treat this thread's audit-recorded apply as already applied on a fresh source), and the tests check that behaviour plus thread and key scoping that follows from it.
The text states the 200-character cut, and the test only checks that a long message is truncated.
The task describes in detail the GitHub link attributes and accessible name, the removed resume controls, the footer links and the hero.codeLine the tests check.
Asking for the report as plain text (no --json-schema) and recording the reply's result field follows naturally from the task.
The task title says a recorded fetch error must read exactly like the live one, and the test checks for the same ValueError type and text in record and replay.
The three behaviours are stated, and the tool name 'model' and the type-name detail follow existing conventions in nodes/evidence.py and ask_model.
The task describes replacing the inline grid-template-columns with literal per-count classes and keeping the existing mobile grid-cols classes, which is what the tests check.
The text says the close commit must also include .workhorse/instincts, which is exactly what the test checks.

The task spells out the binary skip that counts skips and fails closed, the @2x, 11x and 4-of-4 boundary rules and the 26-to-29 pin; the one doubt is whether counts.skippedAsBinary already exists in the shared scanner.
Making applied nullable (still required) and adding the effect_unknown escalation reason is stated, and the tests check exactly that.
Making the existing hard-line rules see past git's global options (-C, -c, --git-dir, --no-pager) is exactly what the task says, and the tests reuse the existing line numbers.
The task describes the fail-closed behaviour precisely (render every page in memory, write nothing on a later page's error), and the test checks exactly that.
The test checks that a metric no run scored on either side is left out of the case and totals, while a metric scored before and missing after still fails, which is exactly the rule the task states.
Rendering the existing ContactFooter on NotFoundPage gives the #contact element the test checks.
The text names the new `approval` evidence key, says it holds the decision, and gives the fallback keyed on the idempotency key; the tests check exactly that behaviour.
The text names the unreadable_sources field and the no-range-is-unhealthy rule, and the other tests pin behaviour that already exists.
The text names the log command and its stamping, the existing conductor convention gives the timestamp, phase order, and refusing an empty message is a natural requirement.
Rendering the existing CaseStudyCards and ContactFooter in place of the filter UI gives the links and absences the tests check.
The codeLink label 'Code: agentops-snapshot' and the snapshot URL follow the existing WorkHorse pattern the task points to.
The task describes exactly two footer links and an aria-label built from codeLink.label, which is what the tests assert.
The test races two decide calls and expects one Refused with in_flight/409 and one apply, matching the task's stated reason and status.
Extending the existing pattern to accept the Oxford comma is exactly what the task says, and the near-miss cases follow naturally.
cleanPrompt already exists and the task says plainly to show the <note> text of a <relay> envelope as the prompt.
The task names the aria-disabled approach that keeps focus, and the tests check that attribute and that focus stays.
Removing plan step 4's missing-facts sentence from the existing Orion data is locatable in the repo, and the test only checks that its words are gone.
The title states the behaviour (a plain repeat of an applied key records applied=False so verify escalates), and the test checks only that.
The task says the kill endpoint takes the reason as a query parameter with no body, which is exactly what the test sends.
The text specifies {name, value} pairs in the JSON schema, conversion to a mapping, and refusal of missing, extra or repeated keys, which is what the tests check.
The test checks that record mode serves a prompt it already holds instead of calling the model again, which is the stated behaviour.
The source fix is the one-line empty max() crash the task describes; the test drives existing load-tool behaviour (backoff constant, dollar-formatted report).
The tests check that the education box no longer renders and that exactly one replay step pane is shown at a time, both following from the task.

The task states the ask-versus-refuse behaviour and the 'spend API credit' wording; the permissionDecision 'ask' output is the harness's standard field, and an 'ask' flag on the hit is a natural name.
YAML double-quote escapes and single-quote doubling are specified, and the tests check those behaviours.

The task describes the hover behaviour closely (plate-level hover, settle delay, off-part grace period), the classes the tests use likely already exist, and the test timing windows allow reasonable delay choices.
Not merging the same post-action world twice is clearly described, and the test checks for no duplicate log ids or metric points.
'Label by applies, not loops' clearly means two or more applies, which is what the tests check.
Banning the plain word 'Paddock' as a whole-word, case-insensitive term and removing its data follows directly from the task, and the existing 'Paddock retirement wording' term stays.
